headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Perplexity’s browser-based search outputs feeding Plane’s file/task workflows; no direct shared-channel evidence, so interaction risk is inferred.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity runs live web search and browser-based browsing, so it can surface attacker-controlled content; Plane ingests issues, notes, hyperlinks, and file uploads. If Plane consumes Perplexity output as trusted text, prompt injection is plausible even without a documented shared channel. The pairwise pathway is inferred, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Plane ingests Perplexity-generated text into issue/notes fields without sanitization
IF Perplexity browsing returns adversarial instructions that are copied into Plane
mitigations: Paste Perplexity output into Plane only after stripping instructions and markup
Add a one-line provenance note to every imported snippet
Disable automatic task creation from raw search summaries
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-detection on import

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context, while Plane handles files, notes, and hyperlinks. If users move Perplexity outputs or uploaded content into Plane, sensitive material can persist in a second system with different retention and access controls. No direct shared workspace is documented, so this is inferred but still plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF uploaded documents from Perplexity are copied into Plane file uploads or notes
IF Plane retains imported content longer than the source workflow expects
mitigations: Avoid copying sensitive uploads from Perplexity into Plane
Redact secrets before creating Plane issues from search results
Set a short retention policy for imported attachments
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity has no filesystem write, no git modification, and vendor-only egress; Plane also has no filesystem write and no elevated scopes. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is broad content handling and API use, so the main risk is coordination friction rather than destructive contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external task source and users expect synchronized writes
IF Plane is self-hosted with additional write integrations not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign one system as the source of truth for task state
Use manual approval before copying outputs between systems
Avoid concurrent edits to the same issue or note
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency on shared records

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from live search, and Plane is an issue/task system that can turn imported text into work items. If Plane treats Perplexity output as authoritative, a mistaken summary can cascade into incorrect tasks or roadmap decisions. The interaction is not directly documented, so I choose medium rather than low because the default workflow can propagate errors.
conditions: IF Plane users create tasks directly from Perplexity summaries without verification
IF downstream assignees act on imported claims as facts
mitigations: Require a human verification step before task creation
Attach source links to every imported claim
Mark imported items as unverified until reviewed
requires-engineering: add citation-checking or review gates before task conversion

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context, while Plane can be self-hosted but also exposes file uploads and external support channels. If regulated data is moved from Perplexity into Plane, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a compliance-risk inference, not a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded to Perplexity and then copied into Plane
IF the Plane deployment uses retention or residency settings different from the source workflow
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both systems unless approved
Document the data class allowed in each system
Set deletion/retention reminders for imported records
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and DPA controls across deployments
